V5 WHY NINE MECHANISMS FAILED, RECONCILED
Rape 2006: processivity is 'strongly influenced by the D box within the substrate'.
loop 146 selected every class starting with DEG_, so the D box was INSIDE its tested set: True
loop 146 measured occupancy gain REQUIRED {'Q1': True, 'Q2': True, 'Q3': False, 'Q4': False, 'Q5': False, 'Q6': True}

this repo tested the right motif for the wrong PROPERTY. Loops 121, 145 and 146 asked whether a substrate HAS a D box; Rape 2006 says every APC substrate has one and what orders them is how PROCESSIVELY that box is engaged -- a graded kinetic quantity a regex cannot see. A presence test would fail even when the mechanism is exactly right, which is what happened. That reconciles the failures rather than explaining them away, and it predicts the oscillators differ in D box QUALITY and not in whether they have one.
V6 WHAT THE LITERATURE DOES NOT GIVE US
processivity in Rape 2006 and Lu 2015 is measured in vitro on a handful of substrates -- cyclin A, cyclin B, geminin, securin, Nek2A. It is not proteome-wide and
there is no table of processivity per gene to join against the 77 oscillators.
So this loop does NOT identify which proteins are distributive. The arc's central question -- WHICH proteins are destroyed on schedule -- is not closed by these papers.
What they close is different and still worth having: the mechanism class is real and measured rather than derived, loop 151's cost objection rested on a premise the
literature contradicts, and nine failures have an explanation that predicts something rather than merely excusing them.
